title: Observe installed Claude runtime from production Windows facts
description: Objective: supply the missing production host adapter behind Claude runtime pinning. Fresh measurement at committed HEAD 6ca5da07 found `probeClaudeRuntime` and `prepareClaudeRuntimePin`, but no production `ClaudeProbePort`/`ClaudeRuntimeFactsPort`; all callers are tests or recovery inventory, while task-6cbff010 can currently succeed only by injecting `{fs,facts,clock}` from its test. Deliverable: an internal @moe/runner Windows host module that takes only bounded plain installed-runtime configuration, resolves and streams the complete native Claude closure, obtains version and platform facts through a shell-free bounded Windows process/OS boundary, feeds the production capability/observation builders, and returns immutable current facts/observation or an existing stable RUNTIME/Windows-process refusal. Unproven capabilities remain UNSUPPORTED. No caller-supplied observation, digest, version, capability answer, filesystem capability, clock, or process seam may become authority. This producer is consumed by task 6f8f1e5c (server-owned pin-request hydration; create immediately after this task) and ultimately task-6cbff010. NOT in scope: grant consumption, daemon/store orchestration, provider work launch, review, or final acceptance. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-host-runtime.ts, claude-host-runtime.js, and claude-host-runtime.test.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: On Windows, the production adapter resolves a bounded local installed root/executable, streams closure digests, performs a shell-free bounded version/facts observation, and returns a production-built immutable ProviderRuntimeObservation plus ClaudeRuntimeFacts whose digest and truth class recompute.

Malformed, non-Windows, missing/reparse/escaping, unreadable, timed-out, malformed-output, and drifted observations fail closed with the exact existing RUNTIME or Windows-process reason code and refusing layer; no case upgrades UNKNOWN/UNSUPPORTED to PROVEN.
Only capabilities proved by the production observation are SUPPORTED; a version-only probe leaves every other capability explicitly UNSUPPORTED, with generated cases asserting a positive count.

Tests exercise the production surface and include a real Windows conformance leg (native Windows or `/init` bridge) plus mutation drills proving closure hashing, fresh version/platform facts, and fail-closed classification are load-bearing.
All three owned files are the only changed paths, each production source is below 250 physical lines, and runner/repo typecheck plus a nonzero runner test suite pass.
taskRails: Use the existing `probeClaudeRuntime`, observation builder, runtime-pin filesystem, and Windows process boundary internally; do not reimplement their authority or publish their injectable ports.
The public result may expose facts/data, never filesystem/process/clock capabilities; input is bounded plain data and error messages do not echo runtime paths, argv, environment, or secrets.
TDD every behavior; every failure test asserts exact stable reason code and layer, generated sweeps assert a positive case count, and mutation drills target the production surface.
Keep the TypeScript production file below 250 physical lines, the .js bridge one line, and commit only the three explicit owned paths.

VOCABULARIES READ OFF DISK, not from memory:
- `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_LAYER` = "RUNTIME"; `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_ERROR_CODES` (16): PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED, QUOTE_INVALID, PATH_INVALID, PATH_MISSING, PATH_NOT_FILE, PATH_DUPLICATE, PATH_REPARSE, PATH_ESCAPE, SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH, PIN_COLLISION, PIN_COPY_FAILED, PIN_DESTINATION_MISMATCH, PIN_SOURCE_DRIFT, PIN_CLEANUP_FAILED, OBSERVATION_CHANGED, OBSERVATION_INVALID (all prefixed CLAUDE_RUNTIME_).

MEASURED GAP worth flagging now: this failure shape is `ClaudeFailure {ok,code,message}` and carries NO layer field, and there is no CLAUDE_OBSERVATION_LAYER constant anywhere. The three-layer refusal union therefore discriminates by code prefix for this arm; RUNTIME and WINDOWS_PROCESS both carry a real `layer`. I will assert layer wherever one exists and assert the code-prefix plus absence of a layer for the observation arm rather than inventing a layer constant.
- `WINDOWS_PROCESS_LAYERS` (6): WINDOWS_PROCESS_REQUEST, WINDOWS_PROCESS_RESOLUTION, WINDOWS_PROCESS_TRANSPORT, BROKER_DESCRIPTOR, BROKER_PROTOCOL, BROKER_NATIVE. `WINDOWS_PROCESS_CODES` includes PROCESS_BOUNDARY_LAUNCH_TIMED_OUT, PROCESS_BOUNDARY_BROKER_UNRESOLVED, PROCESS_BOUNDARY_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED, and the framing/transport family.

- Launch request shape for the boundary is exactly `{executable, argv, cwd, environment}` (windows-launch-request.ts:62), `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` is 30 minutes, and the boundary is synchronous on its refusal path returning `WindowsProcessBoundary | WindowsProcessUnknown`.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED FIRST — write the refusal sweep before any production byte. Create `packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-host-runtime.test.ts` importing the not-yet-existing `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime` from `./claude-host-runtime.js`, and watch it fail to resolve. Then write the fail-closed cases, EVERY one asserting BOTH the exact stable code AND the refusing layer — never merely 'not ok', because three different layers can refuse here (RUNTIME via claude-runtime-pin-closure, the observation builder's CLAUDE_OBSERVATION_* codes, and WINDOWS_PROCESS_* at its own layer) and a code-only assertion silently detaches the moment a different layer starts answering first.
Cases: non-Windows platform; malformed input (not an object, missing keys, extra keys, non-string paths, oversized path text); a candidate path that is missing, a directory, a reparse point, or escapes the containment root; an unreadable file; a version probe that times out; malformed version output; and a closure that drifts between the two inspection passes. Map each to the measured member you pinned in step 1 — for example escape/reparse/missing map to `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_ESCAPE` / `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_REPARSE` / `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_MISSING` at layer RUNTIME, drift maps to `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_SOURCE_DRIFT`, and a boundary timeout maps to `PROCESS_BOUNDARY_LAUNCH_TIMED_OUT` at its Windows layer.
Build each fixture so it is VALID AT EVERY EARLIER LAYER and only the property under test is wrong; otherwise an earlier guard answers and the assertion quietly stops testing its subject. Keep ALL fixtures and helpers in this test file — the 250-line cap binds the production source, not the test, and the three owned paths leave you no fourth file for fixtures. Assert that NO refusal case yields truthClass PROVEN or any capability SUPPORTED.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED first, confirmed before any production byte existed: `pnpm --filter @moe/runner exec vitest run --root ../.. packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-host-runtime.test.ts` -> EXIT 1, `Cannot find module './claude-host-runtime.js'`, `packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-host-runtime.test.ts (0 test)`.

The entry is resolved through the module NAMESPACE, copying the idiom claude-runtime-source.test.ts documents: a missing named import fails the file to load and reports ZERO executed tests, which is indistinguishable from a suite that tested nothing. Through the namespace, every case executes and fails on its own assertion.

16 fail-closed cases on win32 (9 off it), each asserting the exact code AND the layer, with a `CASES.length` assertion so a silently emptied sweep reddens. RUNTIME-layer cases: input not a record / a string / an array / omitting the executable / carrying an extra key (`fs`, the exact seam this module refuses to accept) / a non-string executable / a non-positive timeout, all CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_INVALID; oversized and relative path text, CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_INVALID; missing, directory, junction-crossing and root-escaping candidates, CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_MISSING / _NOT_FILE / _REPARSE / _ESCAPE. WINDOWS-layer case: a real file that is not a loadable image, PROCESS_BOUNDARY_BROKER_REFUSED at BROKER_NATIVE — a case where every runtime-layer rule passes so the Windows layer is provably the one that answered. Every refusal is additionally asserted to carry no observation, no profile, and never truthClass PROVEN.

Fixtures are valid at every earlier layer by construction: the reparse case uses a real directory junction (no Administrator rights needed, and the segment walk rejects a reparse point anywhere in the path), the escape case is a real readable file in a second real root, and the not-an-image case is a real readable file with real bytes.

THREE MEASURED CORRECTIONS to the plan's predicted mappings — measured on this host through the real broker before writing the assertions, because writing them from the plan would have pinned behavior that does not exist:
1. A short probe timeout does NOT produce PROCESS_BOUNDARY_LAUNCH_TIMED_OUT. Measured with timeoutMs=1: the broker still delivers a terminal status frame, so the outcome is `truthClass: "PROVEN"` with `exitCode: 1` and empty stdout. LAUNCH_TIMED_OUT is only the fallback when the broker exits WITHOUT a terminal frame after a timeout cancellation (windows-boundary-session.ts:220). So the timed-out case is asserted as what production really does: CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_INVALID at RUNTIME, the module refusing because no version was observed.
2. `boundary.completed` does not resolve at child exit for this provider — measured at 4s, 20s and 30s bounds, it resolves at the TIMEOUT every time (claude.exe leaves the job non-empty), while `close()` right after stdout ends settles in ~112ms. That is the same root cause as the foreign claude-launcher.windows.test.ts red. Awaiting `completed` is still the correct bounded contract, so a successful probe costs its timeout; the suite therefore uses a 4s probe bound and a 60s per-case bound.
3. Waiting on stdout `end` alone HANGS when the launch is refused (no process, so no stream end). Measured: the first probe shape deadlocked. Production awaits `completed`, which settles on both paths.

Also measured, and the reason the "unrecognised version output" case is honest rather than synthetic: node.exe answers `--version` with `v24.16.0` and exits 0 — a clean execution whose output is not the shape this provider reports (`2.1.233 (Claude Code)`), so it exercises the parse refusal rather than an exit-code refusal.

implementationPlan.description:
PRODUCTION PART 1 — module skeleton, platform gate, bounded input. Create `packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-host-runtime.ts` and its one-line bridge `claude-host-runtime.js` containing exactly `export * from "./claude-host-runtime.ts";` with an LF ending (copy the byte pattern from a sibling such as claude-runtime-source.js; the repo's bridge guard byte-compares, so CRLF or a trailing blank line is a failure).
Public surface: an input interface of BOUNDED PLAIN DATA ONLY — the installed root, the single native executable path, and an optional timeout number. No `fs`, no `facts`, no `clock`, no `port`, no process seam may appear in the input or the result; that injectability is precisely the gap this task closes, and re-exposing it would reproduce the defect. Export one async entry, `observeInstalledClaudeRuntime(input: unknown)`, returning either an ok record carrying `observation` (ProviderRuntimeObservation), `facts` (ClaudeRuntimeFacts) and `profile` (ClaudeCapabilityProfile), or an existing refusal union.
First gate, before any I/O or import-time cost: `process.platform !== "win32"` returns the existing RUNTIME refusal `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED` via the existing `refuse` helper from claude-runtime-pin-closure.ts — do not mint a new code or a new layer. Then harden the input into a frozen plain snapshot and build exactly ONE candidate, `{ kind: "EXECUTABLE", path }`, passed through the existing `snapshotSourceCandidates` from claude-runtime-source.ts. The supported closure for v1 is that one explicitly named native executable — do NOT call `listFiles()`, whose recursive walk materializes an unbounded array. Error messages must not echo runtime paths, argv, environment, or secrets.
implementationPlan.note:
Module and bridge created. `od -c claude-host-runtime.js` is exactly `export * from "./claude-host-runtime.ts";\n` (41 bytes, single LF, no trailing blank), byte-compared against the sibling claude-runtime-source.js pattern before writing and written in binary mode so no CRLF could creep in.

PUBLIC SURFACE, bounded plain data only: `InstalledClaudeRuntimeInput { installedRoot, executablePath, versionTimeoutMs? }` and `ObservedInstalledClaudeRuntime { ok, observation, facts, profile }`, with `ObserveInstalledClaudeRuntimeResult` unioning that against the three EXISTING refusal shapes — ClaudeRuntimePinFailure (RUNTIME), ClaudeFailure<ClaudeObservationErrorCode>, and WindowsProcessUnknown. No fs, facts port, clock, probe port or process seam appears in the input or the result; the probe port and the node fs port are both constructed inside the module. A test case deliberately passes `{ ..., fs: {} }` and asserts it is refused, so the seam's absence is asserted rather than merely intended.

PLATFORM GATE FIRST, before any path is read or any seam is touched: `process.platform !== "win32"` returns the existing `refuse("CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED", ...)` — no new code, no new layer.

INPUT HARDENING: `snapshotExactRecord` twice (3-key, then the 2-key required set) because that helper demands an exact key count, which is how the optional timeout stays optional while an extra key is still refused. Descriptor-based lifting means no accessor is ever invoked. Paths go through the existing `pathShapeRejection`, the timeout must be a positive safe integer bounded at 600000ms, and the result is frozen before any I/O so nothing the caller still holds can change a validated path.

EXACTLY ONE CANDIDATE, `{ kind: "EXECUTABLE", path }`, through the existing `snapshotSourceCandidates`. `listFiles()` is not called anywhere in this module — its recursive walk materializes an unbounded array, and the supported v1 closure is the one explicitly named native executable.

MESSAGES ECHO NOTHING: every refusal message is a fixed sentence about the category ("an installed runtime path ...", "the closure changed while the version probe ran"). No path, argv, environment value or secret is interpolated into any message this module produces.

implementationPlan.description:
PRODUCTION PART 2 — validated streamed closure, twice, with drift detection. Use `inspectSources(fs, candidates, realRoot)` from claude-runtime-source.ts with an `fs` obtained from `createNodeClaudeRuntimeFs()` (claude-runtime-pin-fs.ts:61), constructed INSIDE this module and never accepted from the caller. This is the primitive task-ff589abd was created to deliver, and it is the reason this task was blocked: it performs the segment/reparse/containment walk and returns the streamed `sha256` in one pass, so you never hash a candidate before validating it. Do NOT copy the private segment walk into this module — that would create parallel authority and violate task rail 1.
Run the inspection TWICE, once before the version probe of step 5 and once after, and require the resulting `SourceEntry` digests to be identical. A mismatch returns `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_SOURCE_DRIFT`. The two-pass shape is the point: a single pass cannot tell a stable installation from one swapped underneath you while the probe was running, and DoD 2 requires drifted observations to fail closed. Feed the second pass's entries — not the first's — into the observation as `resolvedRuntimeClosure`, so the bytes reported are the bytes that survived the probe window.
implementationPlan.note:
Closure inspection composed, twice, through the primitive ff589abd delivered — never re-derived. `inspectClosure` calls `inspectSources(fs, quoted, realRoot)` with `fs = createNodeClaudeRuntimeFs()` constructed inside the module; `expectedSha256` is null because this adapter OBSERVES a digest rather than checking one a caller declared. No segment walk, reparse check, containment check or digest loop is reimplemented here — a grep of this module for `realpath`, `entryKind`, `readChunks` or `streamDigest` finds only the single `fs.realpath(installedRoot)` used to resolve the containment root itself.

TWO PASSES, before and after the probe, compared by `digestsOf` over `relativePath:sha256` of every entry; a mismatch returns CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_SOURCE_DRIFT at RUNTIME. The SECOND pass's entries are what feed `resolvedRuntimeClosure`, so the bytes reported are the bytes that survived the probe window.

ORDERING CORRECTION worth recording, found by the drift test rather than by reading. My first cut parsed the version text immediately after the probe and returned before the second pass ran, so a drifting closure whose probe output was also unparseable answered CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_INVALID instead of the drift code — the test caught exactly the "an earlier guard answers and the assertion stops testing its subject" failure the plan warns about. The probe now returns RAW text, the second pass and the drift comparison run BEFORE the output is classified, and the parse happens last. That order is also the more honest one: if the bytes changed under the observation, output attributed to them must not be classified at all, not even as a bad version.

Drift is proven by a real swap, not a fake: the test starts the observation against a real executable copy, waits 750ms while the boundary holds its bound open, renames the running image aside (legal on Windows; deleting it is not) and writes different bytes at the same path. Measured result CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_SOURCE_DRIFT at RUNTIME. Suite: 19 passed (19), runner typecheck exit 0.

implementationPlan.description:
PRODUCTION PART 3 — shell-free bounded version observation through the real Job boundary. Obtain the reported version by launching the validated executable with a single `--version` argument through `openWindowsProcessBoundary(request, { timeoutMs })` from platform/windows/windows-boundary.ts. That is the production Windows process seam: it is broker-mediated, job-object bounded, and structurally shell-free — do NOT reach for child_process, a shell, or `.cmd`/`.bat` indirection. Note the boundary is SYNCHRONOUS on its refusal path and returns `WindowsProcessBoundary | WindowsProcessUnknown`; a `WindowsProcessUnknown` is already a stable coded refusal at its own layer, so return it unchanged rather than re-wrapping it into a RUNTIME code and erasing which layer answered.
On the success path, read `providerStdout` with a BOUNDED accumulation (cap the bytes you retain, matching the existing `MAX_RUNTIME_TEXT_CHARS` discipline in claude-observation.ts) and await `completed`; always `close()` the boundary on every exit path including the throw path, so a failed parse cannot leak a broker process. Parse the version text conservatively — a shape you do not recognise yields a refusal, never a guessed string and never null-as-success. Pass an explicit bounded `timeoutMs`; the module's `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` is 30 minutes, far too long for a version probe.
Separately derive `PlatformIdentity` — `{os, arch, osVersion}` — from `node:os` inside this module, then validate it through the EXISTING `platformHostRejection` / `readHostIdentity` / `MAX_PLATFORM_IDENTITY_CHARS` helpers in platform/platform-contract.ts rather than writing your own bounds check. There is no `observeWindowsPlatform` producer in this repo (measured: linux-observation.ts and macos-observation.ts exist, no Windows sibling); reading `node:os` here is the production host boundary, and the clock is likewise constructed internally, never injected.
implementationPlan.note:
Version observation runs through the real Job boundary and nothing else. `openWindowsProcessBoundary({executable, argv: ["--version"], cwd: installedRoot, environment}, {timeoutMs})`. This module imports no `node:child_process`, spawns nothing, and names no `.cmd`/`.bat`; the broker is the only process seam it can reach.

REFUSAL PATH RETURNED UNCHANGED: the boundary is synchronous when it refuses, so `if (!("providerStdout" in boundary)) return boundary` hands back the WindowsProcessUnknown with its own code and its own layer intact. The test proves the layer survives — a real non-image file answers PROCESS_BOUNDARY_BROKER_REFUSED at BROKER_NATIVE, not a RUNTIME restamp.

BOUNDED, DRAINED, ALWAYS CLOSED: stdout is accumulated only while `text.length < MAX_RUNTIME_TEXT_CHARS` (the existing 400-char discipline), stderr is drained with `resume()` so an unread pipe cannot stall the broker, and `close()` runs in a `finally` so a failed parse or a throw cannot leak a broker process. The version is taken from the FIRST line only.

CONSERVATIVE PARSE: `isBoundedLabel(text) && VERSION_PATTERN.test(text)` where the pattern is `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:[-+.][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?(?:\s+\(.{1,100}\))?$` — matching the real `2.1.233 (Claude Code)` and refusing anything else. Never a guess, never null-as-success: an unrecognised shape returns CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_INVALID.

TIMEOUT: explicit, default 10s, bounded at 600000ms, replacing the boundary's 30-minute default. Two measured facts shape this and both are worth carrying forward. First, `completed` resolves at the TIMEOUT rather than at child exit for this provider (measured at 4s/20s/30s bounds; the job stays non-empty), so a successful probe costs its bound — awaiting `completed` is still right because it is the only settled contract, and the caller controls the cost. Second, waiting on stdout `end` instead HANGS forever when the launch is refused, because a stream that never opened never ends; the first shape I measured deadlocked exactly there.

ENVIRONMENT is an allowlisted snapshot of SYSTEMROOT and PATH only, read inside the module, and never echoed into any message.

PLATFORM IDENTITY: `{os: process.platform, arch: arch(), osVersion: release()}` read from `node:os` here — measured, there is no `observeWindowsPlatform` producer in this repo — then validated through the EXISTING `readHostIdentity` (the same authority `platformHostRejection` wraps), refusing CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_INVALID if it is not bounded normalized text. The clock is likewise internal: `{ observedAt: () => new Date().toISOString() }`. Neither is injectable.

implementationPlan.description:
PRODUCTION PART 4 — compose capabilities, observation, and facts from what was actually proved. Build a `ClaudeProbeReport` (claude-capabilities.ts:97) populated ONLY from this run's evidence: `resolvedRuntimeClosure` from the second inspection pass, `reportedVersion` from the probe, `pinningMethod` set to `CONTENT_ADDRESSED_COPY` (a validated native executable closure can be content-addressed and copied — assert in the test that it is NOT `UNSUPPORTED`, since that member exists precisely so a wrapper can read a definite negative). EVERY other field — structuredSample, rawSampleBase64, cancelObservation, processTreeObservation, runEnumeration, tokenizer, declaredContextLimit, helpText, resumeClaim — stays null. A version-only probe proves version and pin method and nothing else.
Wrap that report in a `ClaudeProbePort` constructed internally and pass it to the existing `probeClaudeRuntime({ port, clock, platformIdentity })` (claude-probe.ts:56), which runs `assessCapabilities` and `buildProviderRuntimeObservation` for you. Do not call the builders directly around it and do not re-implement their authority — task rail 1. Note the port is INTERNAL: it must not appear on this module's public surface.
Derive `ClaudeRuntimeFacts` (claude-runtime-pin.ts:41) as `{ platformIdentity, reportedVersion, adapterCapabilitySchemaDigest }`, taking the digest from the profile's `capabilitySchemaDigest` — never from caller input. Freeze the returned observation and facts. The expected outcome, which the tests must pin as an exact set rather than a spot check: of the ELEVEN members of `CLAUDE_CAPABILITIES`, exactly TWO are SUPPORTED — `PIN_METHOD` (proof `PIN_METHOD_RECORD`) and `VERSION_REPORT` (proof `VERSION_RECORD`) — and the remaining NINE are UNSUPPORTED with proof `NONE`, with `contextPolicy` HOLD_UNKNOWN because no limit was declared. Assert the SUPPORTED count is exactly 2 and the UNSUPPORTED count exactly 9, and assert the records equal the full eleven-member vocabulary in vocabulary order — a sweep that generates zero cases, or that spot-checks two members, passes while testing nothing.
implementationPlan.note:
Composed THROUGH `probeClaudeRuntime({port, clock, platformIdentity})`, never around it. `assessCapabilities` and `buildProviderRuntimeObservation` are not called from this module at all — a grep finds neither name here — so their authority stays in one place.

`versionOnlyReport` carries only this run's evidence: `resolvedRuntimeClosure` mapped from the SECOND inspection pass (kind, canonicalPath, sha256), `reportedVersion` from the probe, `pinningMethod: "CONTENT_ADDRESSED_COPY"` because a validated native executable closure genuinely can be content-addressed and copied. implementationPlan.note:
Three drills, each run alone and reverted before the next, each landing RED on the intended assertion.

FIRST, a test strengthening the drills forced. The conformance leg originally asserted the closure digest matched `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` and that `reportedVersion` was non-null — both of which a constant would satisfy, so neither drill 1 nor drill 2 could have reddened anything. Added two INDEPENDENT oracles: the digest is compared against `createHash("sha256").update(readFileSync(executable))` computed in the test, and the version is compared against a direct `execFileSync(executable, ["--version"])`. Both are independent observations of the same real file, not reimplementations of production authority. This is the "a green drill may indict the mutation, or the test" case: the drill exposed a weak assertion, and the assertion was fixed.

DRILL 1 — CLOSURE HASHING. File packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-runtime-pin-fs.ts, function `streamDigest`, exact replaced range: `for await (const chunk of fs.readChunks(path)) {\n    hash.update(chunk);\n  }` -> the same loop with `break;` added after `hash.update(chunk)`, so only the first 65536-byte chunk is hashed. RED on the intended assertion: `AssertionError: the closure digest is not the real bytes of the real file: expected 'be21097a6e20964c67c7a3b6d2a093243cab5...' to be '8ae35d41252b02a7b747097ececf368b6872fab93ca104832b99a8ec5942fabd'`. The digest is streamed from the whole real file, not echoed. Restored with `git checkout -- packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-runtime-pin-fs.ts` (tracked, so the checkout is exact) and verified by sha256sum against the pre-drill baseline: OK.

DRILL 2 — FRESH FACTS. File claude-host-runtime.ts, `probeVersionText`, exact replaced range: `return text.split("\n")[0]?.trim() ?? "";` -> `return text.length >= 0 ? "2.1.999 (Claude Code)" : "";` — a plausible constant of exactly the right shape, deliberately NOT the true version, because substituting the true one would be an honest equivalent mutant no test could distinguish. RED on the intended assertion: `the reported version is not what the runtime really prints: expected '2.1.999 (Claude Code)' to be '2.1.233 (Claude Code)'`. Restored by inverse edit, sha256sum -c OK.

DRILL 3 — FAIL-CLOSED CLASSIFICATION. File claude-host-runtime.ts, `reportedVersionOf`, exact replaced range: `isBoundedLabel(text) && VERSION_PATTERN.test(text)` -> `isBoundedLabel(text) || !VERSION_PATTERN.test(text)`, so unrecognised output falls through to the ok path.
